title: Inference Economics Translator for Sales and Security
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This page is a compact, field-ready briefing designed to help Redwood sellers and solutions engineers translate technical inference trade-offs (latency, throughput, cost, reliability) into buyer-focused outcomes for platform, security, and finance stakeholders. Use it as a one-page narrative, a checklist for discovery calls, and a quick reference during pricing negotiations and pilot scoping.

Audience:
- Sales reps and SEs engaging platform engineering, security/compliance, ML engineering, and procurement teams.

Elevator pitch (1 line):
Redwood makes model inference predictable and economical at production scale by exposing measurable levers — batching, caching, quantization, and routing — backed by SLA-aware deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).

Positioning summary (3 bullets):
- Production-first: we prioritize predictable latency and unit economics for real applications, not benchmarks.
- Deployment parity: same API and rollout primitives across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private so customers avoid refactoring as they scale.
- Cost controls and observability: token-level attribution, per-route cost breakdowns, and automated recommendations reduce TCO while preserving model quality.

Messaging by buyer persona (talk tracks and proof points):
1) Platform Engineer
- Pain: unpredictable tail latency, noisy neighbors, hard capacity planning.
- Talk track: show routing policies + Dedicated capacity. Demonstrate our 99th percentile SLOs and autoscaling controls.
- Proof points: Dedicated pools with per-tenant GPU pinning; configurable autoscale window (1–60s); tracing hooks for request-level latency.

2) ML Engineer
- Pain: quality regressions when optimizing for cost.
- Talk track: we support model variants and canary rollouts with automatic fallback to higher-fidelity variants when metrics degrade.
- Proof points: integrated evals tied to prompt sets, automated quality regression alerts.

3) Security/Compliance
- Pain: data residency, auditability, key management.
- Talk track: Private deployments with customer-controlled control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and retention controls.
- Proof points: audit logs, SOC-like evidence package, optional on-prem runtime.

4) CFO/Procurement
- Pain: unclear unit economics and hidden run costs.
- Talk track: present per-token and per-embedding pricing, reserved capacity discounts, and modeled savings for batching/caching.
- Proof points: sample pricing scenarios (see Pricing Guidance).

Competitive brief (concise):
- AWS/GCP managed endpoints: strength = integrated infra, weakness = limited model optimizations and higher per-token cost for LLM-like workflows. Redwood differentiator: inference runtime optimized for attention and KV cache management, with explicit batching/caching levers exposed.
- LLM API providers (pure hosted): strength = simplicity, weakness = vendor lock and limited deployment modes. Redwood differentiator: same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; predictable performance tiers.
- Self-hosted inference vendors: strength = control, weakness = heavy ops burden. Redwood differentiator: full ops-surface + optional Private deployment plus enterprise support and rollout tooling.

Pricing guidance (field-ready examples):
Assumptions: baseline model = 70B dense, average prompt+response = 120 tokens, 20% prefix reuse across requests.
Scenario A — Small pilot (Hosted):
- Volume: 500k tokens/month
- Pricing: Hosted generation $0.0008 per token (example list price)
- Monthly cost: 500,000 * 0.0008 = $400
- Quick win messaging: low initial cost, no infra commitment, fast time-to-value.

Scenario B — Production throughput (Dedicated) with batching & caching:
- Volume: 200M tokens/month
- Reserved capacity: 1x P4d-equivalent pool (predictable throughput) — commit: $40k/month (example committed price)
- Effective per-token after autoscale and batching: ~ $0.00012/token (estimated with 8x batching + 20% KV hit-rate)
- Monthly cost (approx): 200M * 0.00012 = $24,000 (plus reserved capacity adjustments)
- Delta vs Hosted: >40% cost reduction at scale when batching and cache apply.

Negotiation levers to offer/ask for pilot-to-prod:
- Time-limited reserved capacity discount for 3–6 month pilot commits.
- Extended observability retention during pilot (e.g., 90 days) as part of pilot package.
- Performance SLA trial (e.g., 99th percentile latency SLO during pilot with credit on breach).
- Model variant credits: fallback to smaller quantized variants in peak traffic windows.

Quick math checklist for discovery (questions to ask):
- Expected QPS, average tokens per request (prompt+response), and peak concurrency.
- Acceptable P99 latency (ms) and throughput vs. cost priorities.
- Data residency and retention constraints.
- Internal policy on KMS/HSM / SOC2 evidence.

Pilot scoping template (use on calls):
1) Objective: e.g., validate sub-200ms P95 for user-facing summarization while keeping per-token cost below $0.0002.
2) Duration: 6 weeks (2 weeks integration, 2 weeks realistic load, 2 weeks analysis + docs).
3) Success criteria: latency P95 < target, model quality pass rate > 95% on evaluation prompt set, unit cost <= target.
4) Deliverables: integration runbook, cost projection workbook, RL-like prompt set for evals, rollback plan.

Technical appendix (field snippets and SLOs):
- Typical SLOs to present: 99.9% availability, P95 latency target (user-facing) 150–300ms depending on model size, P99 latency (background tasks) < 1s.
- Runtime features to call out: continuous batching, KV prefix caching, quantization profiles (int8/4), model variants, automatic fallbacks, per-route tracing.

Example Dedicated capacity YAML (for scoping conversation):
---
pool_name: customer-x-primary
gpu_type: a100-80gb
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 8
autoscale_policy:
  target_rps: 1200
  evaluation_window_seconds: 30
  cooldown_seconds: 60
priority: reserved
---
(Share this as a template to engineering buyers; customize GPU type and replica counts based on projected QPS.)

API example (showing prefix caching hint):
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: {
  "model": "redwood-70b-v2",
  "input": "<user prompt>",
  "cache_hint": {"namespace": "customer-123", "key": "conversation_prefix", "ttl_seconds": 86400}
}

Security FAQ (top prospect questions and short answers):
Q: Can we run Redwood Private in our VPC with our KMS?
A: Yes — Private supports customer-managed control plane and KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSMs via KMIP).

Q: What audit trails are available?
A: Per-request audit logs including request metadata, model version, tokens processed, and response hashes. Logs can be exported to customer SIEM.

Q: How is data retained and purged?
A: Retention windows are configurable per-customer and per-route; we support immediate purge requests via API for restricted datasets.

Q: Do you support on-prem air-gapped installs?
A: Yes — our on-prem package includes an air-gapped deployment mode and documented handoff checklist for security review.

Mini case study (field summary, anonymized):
Customer: "Mid-size marketplaces" (e-commerce platform, ~80M monthly sessions)
Problem: high-latency product search re-ranking and expensive per-inference cost on competitor managed endpoints.
Approach: 8-week pilot using Dedicated pool + prefix cache for repeated cart contexts + quantized retrieval-augmented models.
Outcome: 65% reduction in per-inference CPU/GPU cost for re-ranking, P95 latency improved from 420ms to 190ms, and improved conversion by ~2.1 percentage points in A/B test.

Sales playbook: step-by-step (one-page):
1) Qualify: run Quick Math Checklist; capture tokens/request and P99 latency requirement.
2) Demo: show Console per-route breakdown; run a live generation with tracing enabled.
3) Scope pilot: use Pilot Scoping Template; propose a 6-week pilot.
4) Negotiate: propose reserved capacity discount + extended observability as pilot incentives.
5) Execute: SE owns integration day 0–14; Solutions + Customer Success monitor metrics.
6) Close/Scale: convert pilot commit to Dedicated or Private contract with baseline SLA and rollback controls.

Attachments & artifacts to include with proposal:
- Pilot cost workbook (spreadsheet) with per-token math and sensitivity to cache hit-rate and batching.
- Sample eval prompt set for quality guardrails.
- Dedicated capacity YAML and runbook excerpt.
- Security evidence checklist (SOC-like artifacts).
